comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Checked 2026-10-21 against Deer Valley's terrain-status list (the Lifts & Trails of deervalley.com/explore-the-mountain/mountain-report, from its feed) and the run layer of its interactive trail map (vicomap map 1815, embedded at deervalley.com/explore-the-mountain/interactive-grooming-map). The seven Hail Peak runs opening in 2026-27 (Hill Yeah and others) are on neither yet and stay as mapped. Deer Valley has no terrain park. Where the two agree, their rating is drawn, also where OpenStreetMap rates a run one step harder (Boulder Bumps, Mayflower Bowl). Where they disagree, the harder of their ratings and OpenStreetMap's is kept, so such a run is never drawn easier than any of them (lead's decision 2026-10-22): Silver Buck (Lower) and Blue Bell are blue and Zebra Trees double black. The Deer Crest homeowners' trails by the Jordanelle gondola (Connector, Crest Ridge, Home Run, Lost Fawn, Pioche, Pioche Loop, Ridge Cross, Summit, Town Hall Loop, three short Deer Hollow ways and the private Nelles Loop), on neither the resort's list nor its map, are hidden (lead's decision 2026-10-22).

overrides.reason: Boulder Bumps is blue (intermediate, moguls) on Deer Valley's terrain list and trail map; OSM rates it advanced.
Mayflower Bowl is black (advanced) on Deer Valley's terrain list and trail map (Mayflower Chutes beside it is the double black); OSM rates it expert.
Stein's Way is black (advanced) on Deer Valley's terrain list, and the trail map draws most of it black with a blue lower end; OSM rates the whole way intermediate.

Silver Buck (Lower) is blue (intermediate) on Deer Valley's terrain list, as is Silver Buck (Upper); OSM rates this lower way easy, as the run layer of the interactive trail map draws the section (green). The terrain list is the reference, and where the resort's own sources disagree the harder rating is kept.
